papers.title: Comparison of Colorimetric LAMP and PCR for High-risk HPV Detection: Implications for Cervical Cancer Screening.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cervical cancer, primarily caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, is commonly detected using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based assays. However, these methods are time-consuming and require specialized instrumentation. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay as a rapid alternative for HPV detection compared with conventional PCR testing. METHODS: This study included 933 nonpregnant women aged ≥19 years who underwent HPV testing for cervical cancer screening or follow-up. The HPV panel included 14 high-risk types (16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68). Cervical swab samples underwent nucleic acid extraction followed by LAMP amplification using type-specific primers. Reactions were performed at 63 °C for 35 minutes, and results were interpreted colorimetrically (blue for positive, purple for negative). RESULTS: Compared with PCR, the LAMP assay showed a sensitivity of 97.8% (95% CI: 94.4-100.0) for HPV types 16 and 18 and 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8-100.0) for the remaining high-risk types. Specificity across all types was 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8-100.0). The overall diagnostic accuracy was 99.5% (95% CI: 99.0-100.0). When all 14 HPV types were analyzed collectively, clinical sensitivity and specificity were 99.4% and 100.0%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The LAMP assay provides a rapid, simple, and accurate method for HPV detection and may serve as a useful point-of-care screening tool, particularly in resource-limited settings.

papers.title_zh: 色谱LAMP与PCR在高危型HPV检测中的比较:对宫颈癌筛查的启示。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: Cervical cancer, primarily caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, is commonly detected using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based assays. However, these methods are time-consuming and require specialized instrumentation. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay as a rapid alternative for HPV detection compared with conventional PCR testing. METHODS: This study included 933 nonpregnant women aged ≥19 years who underwent HPV testing for cervical cancer screening or follow-up. The HPV panel included 14 high-risk types (16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, 59, 66, and 68). Cervical swab samples underwent nucleic acid extraction followed by LAMP amplification using type-specific primers. Reactions were performed at 63 °C for 35 minutes, and results were interpreted colorimetrically (blue for positive, purple for negative). RESULTS: Compared with PCR, the LAMP assay showed a sensitivity of 97.8% (95% CI: 94.4-100.0) for HPV types 16 and 18 and 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8-100.0) for the remaining high-risk types. Specificity across all types was 100.0% (95% CI: 98.8-100.0). The overall diagnostic accuracy was 99.5% (95% CI: 99.0-100.0). When all 14 HPV types were analyzed collectively, clinical sensitivity and specificity were 99.4% and 100.0%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The LAMP assay provides a rapid, simple, and accurate method for HPV detection and may serve as a useful point-of-care screening tool, particularly in resource-limited settings.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的:宫颈癌主要由人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒,HPV)感染引起,通常使用基于聚合酶链反应(PCR)的检测方法进行检测。然而,这些方法耗时且需要专门的仪器。本研究评估了环介导等温扩增(LAMP)检测方法作为快速替代方案在HPV检测中的诊断性能,并与传统PCR检测方法进行比较。方法:本研究纳入了933名≥19岁的非妊娠女性,她们接受了宫颈癌筛查或随访的HPV检测。HPV检测面板包括14种高危型(16、18、31、33、35、39、45、51、52、56、58、59、66和68型)。宫颈拭子样本经过核酸提取后,使用型特异性引物进行LAMP扩增。反应在63 °C下进行35分钟,结果通过颜色变化进行解读(蓝色表示阳性,紫色表示阴性)。结果:与PCR相比,LAMP检测方法对HPV 16和18型的敏感性为97.8%(95% CI:94.4-100.0),对其他高危型的敏感性为100.0%(95% CI:98.8-100.0)。所有类型的特异性为100.0%(95% CI:98.8-100.0)。总体诊断准确度为99.5%(95% CI:99.0-100.0)。当对所有14种HPV类型进行整体分析时,临床敏感性和特异性分别为99.4%和100.0%。结论:LAMP检测方法为HPV检测提供了一种快速、简便且准确的方法,可能在资源有限的环境中作为有用的床边筛查工具。

papers.title: Development and Psychometric Validation of the Human Papillomavirus Prevention Health Literacy Scale for College Students in Taiwan.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted virus associated with several types of cancer. Because college students are a high-risk group, understanding their health literacy with regard to HPV prevention is critical. However, no suitable measurement tools are currently available for this purpose. PURPOSE: In this study, an HPV Prevention Health Literacy Scale (HPV-HLS) was developed, and its reliability and validity were assessed. METHODS: A cross-sectional design was used, and the developed scale was validated on a sample of 372 college students from two universities in northern Taiwan and one university in central Taiwan. The initial scale comprised 49 items, developed from qualitative interviews and a literature review. After content validity assessment and item analysis, the scale was refined to 37 items. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted with 150 participants, followed by confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with 222 participants. Concurrent validity and internal consistency reliability were assessed. Data were collected from November 2021 to December 2022. RESULTS: The results of the EFA revealed a two-factor model accounted for 60.30% of the total variation, and those of the CFA demonstrated favorable goodness-of-fit indices (GFI = .81, CFI = .92, TLI = .91, RMSEA = .07, and SRMR = .02). Moreover, the average variance extracted (AVE) for the two factors were .56 and .64, respectively, with corresponding composite reliability (CR) values of .96 and .93, indicating excellent convergent validity. Notably, the AVE surpassed the squared product-moment correlation of the corresponding factors, affirming good discriminant validity. The final iteration of the HPV-HLS comprised 21 items with two subscales: comprehension and evaluation of general information and seeking information from health care professionals. Concurrent validity was found between the proposed scale and the Mandarin Multidimensional Health Literacy Questionnaire ( r = .68, p < .001). The HPV-HLS demonstrated good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .959). CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS FOR FUTURE PRACTICE: After rigorous psychometric testing, the newly developed HPV-HLS demonstrated excellent reliability and validity, establishing it as an objective tool for evaluating HPV prevention health literacy among college students. This HPV-HLS may be used by health care providers and educators to assess health literacy and evaluate the effectiveness of clinical interventions to prevent HPV infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and validate a psychometric tool, the HPV Prevention Health Literacy Scale (HPV-HLS), to assess health literacy related to HPV prevention among college students in Taiwan. The research was conducted using a cross-sectional design with a sample of 372 students from three universities. The scale was developed from qualitative interviews and literature reviews, then refined through content validity assessment and item analysis. The results showed that the final 21-item scale had a two-factor structure with excellent reliability and validity, as evidenced by high composite reliability (CR) values, favorable goodness-of-fit indices, and strong concurrent validity with the Mandarin Multidimensional Health Literacy Questionnaire. The findings establish the HPV-HLS as a reliable and valid tool for evaluating health literacy in HPV prevention, which can inform clinical practice and educational interventions. The study does not report limitations, which may affect the confidence in its conclusions.

papers.title: Acceptability and preference of self-collected vaginal samples for human papillomavirus DNA testing compared with physician-collected Pap smear.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-collected vaginal sampling for human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing provides a promising alternative to physician-collected Pap smears, especially in low-resource settings. However, data on its acceptability and preferences among Filipino women remain limited. This study aimed to assess women's perceptions, experiences, willingness and preferences regarding self-collected vaginal sampling for HPV DNA testing compared with Pap smears. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 592 women. Participants underwent both physician-collected Pap smears and self-collected vaginal sampling for HPV DNA testing. Perceptions were measured using five-point Likert scale questionnaires before and after self-collection. Descriptive statistics were used, and paired and independent Wilcoxon tests were used to compare Likert responses. Willingness to undergo screening was analyzed with Cochran's Q and McNemar tests. Participants' reasons for their preferred screening method were categorized thematically and displayed in stacked bar charts. RESULTS: Self-collection was generally viewed as painless, not uncomfortable, non-embarrassing, and easy and convenient. Acceptability significantly increased after participants performed self-collection (P < 0.001 for pain and discomfort). Compared with Pap smears, self-collection was seen as less embarrassing (P < 0.001), but rated as less easy (P = 0.01) and less convenient (P = 0.004). Most participants preferred physician-administered screening (84.8%) due to trust in medical expertise, and confidence in the procedure's accuracy, safety and cleanliness. CONCLUSIONS: Self-collected vaginal sampling was highly acceptable, yet physician-collected screening remained the preferred method. Improving education, demonstrations, and support for self-collection may enhance the uptake of HPV DNA testing and broaden access to cervical cancer screening in the Philippines.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 自我采集阴道样本用于人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)DNA检测为医生采集的巴氏涂片提供了一种有前景的替代方案,特别是在资源匮乏的环境中。然而,关于菲律宾女性对其可接受性和偏好的数据仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在592名女性中进行了一项横断面研究。参与者接受了医生采集的巴氏涂片和自我采集的阴道样本用于HPV DNA检测。
elements_zh.methods: 感知通过五点李克特量表问卷在自我采样前和后进行测量。使用描述性统计,并采用配对和独立样本威尔科克森检验来比较李克特量表的回答。接受筛查的意愿通过科克兰Q检验和麦克纳马检验进行分析。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 自我采集阴道样本具有高度可接受性,但医生采集的筛查仍然是首选方法。通过改善自我采集的教育、演示和支持,可能提高HPV DNA检测的参与率,并扩大菲律宾宫颈癌筛查的可及性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能通过强调自我采样方法的教育和支持需求,为提高菲律宾HPV DNA检测的接受度并扩大筛查可及性提供策略依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于菲律宾的一个特定人群,未考虑长期依从性或结果。证据强度中等,因为其基于自我报告的感知和偏好。

papers.title: Quercetin, an active component of Qiu's HuaShi decoction, suppresses glycolysis in cervical epithelial cells to reduce HPV infection via modulating the PRKACA/cAMP/PKA/CREB pathway.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is strongly associated with persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) and poses a substantial threat to women's health. Qiu's HuaShi Decoction (QHD) exhibits potential in cervical cancer treatment, yet its underlying mechanism remains unclear. METHODS: Network pharmacology was utilized to screen the core targets of QHD against HPV-associated cervical cancer. The anti-tumor effects of quercetin were evaluated through integrated in vivo and in vitro experiments. Immunofluorescence staining was applied to observe the status of HPV16 infection. Meanwhile, qRT-PCR and western blot were used to detect the mRNA and protein expression levels of HPV16 oncogenes E6 and E7. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used for in situ validation of protein expression in animal tissues. In addition, western blot was performed to quantify the protein levels of key molecules involved in the PRKACA/PKA/CREB axis and core glycolytic regulators. Furthermore, cAMP content, cellular glucose uptake, lactate production and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) and oxygen consumption rate (OCR) were assessed by commercial kits. Additionally, PRKACA overexpression experiments were performed to dissect the regulatory role of PRKACA in quercetin-mediated effects. RESULTS: Network pharmacology analysis identified quercetin and PRKACA as the core targets of QHD for combating HPV-associated cervical cancer. Quercetin inhibited early HPV16 infection, downregulated HPV16 E6/E7 expression, and suppressed cell proliferation. Mechanistically, quercetin reduced intracellular cAMP levels, inactivated the cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling axis, and suppressed the expression of key glycolytic proteins. Consistently, quercetin suppressed glycolytic phenotypes, including reduced glucose uptake, lactate secretion, and ATP production, accompanied by decreased ECAR and restored OCR in cervical epithelial cells. These phenotypic effects were reversed by PRKACA overexpression. CONCLUSIONS: Quercetin exerts its anti-tumor effects against HPV-related cervical cancer by inhibiting PRKACA expression to disrupt cAMP/PKA/CREB/glycolysis signaling axis, providing a molecular basis for the clinical application of QHD.
papers.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects

papers.title_zh: 槲皮素,邱华石汤剂的活性成分,通过调控PRKACA/cAMP/PKA/CREB通路抑制宫颈上皮细胞糖酵解以减少HPV感染。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is strongly associated with persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) and poses a substantial threat to women's health. Qiu's HuaShi Decoction (QHD) exhibits potential in cervical cancer treatment, yet its underlying mechanism remains unclear. METHODS: Network pharmacology was utilized to screen the core targets of QHD against HPV-associated cervical cancer. The anti-tumor effects of quercetin were evaluated through integrated in vivo and in vitro experiments. Immunofluorescence staining was applied to observe the status of HPV16 infection. Meanwhile, qRT-PCR and western blot were used to detect the mRNA and protein expression levels of HPV16 oncogenes E6 and E7. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used for in situ validation of protein expression in animal tissues. In addition, western blot was performed to quantify the protein levels of key molecules involved in the PRKACA/PKA/CREB axis and core glycolytic regulators. Furthermore, cAMP content, cellular glucose uptake, lactate production and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) and oxygen consumption rate (OCR) were assessed by commercial kits. Additionally, PRKACA overexpression experiments were performed to dissect the regulatory role of PRKACA in quercetin-mediated effects. RESULTS: Network pharmacology analysis identified quercetin and PRKACA as the core targets of QHD for combating HPV-associated cervical cancer. Quercetin inhibited early HPV16 infection, downregulated HPV16 E6/E7 expression, and suppressed cell proliferation. Mechanistically, quercetin reduced intracellular cAMP levels, inactivated the cAMP/PKA/CREB signaling axis, and suppressed the expression of key glycolytic proteins. Consistently, quercetin suppressed glycolytic phenotypes, including reduced glucose uptake, lactate secretion, and ATP production, accompanied by decreased ECAR and restored OCR in cervical epithelial cells. These phenotypic effects were reversed by PRKACA overexpression. CONCLUSIONS: Quercetin exerts its anti-tumor effects against HPV-related cervical cancer by inhibiting PRKACA expression to disrupt cAMP/PKA/CREB/glycolysis signaling axis, providing a molecular basis for the clinical application of QHD.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:宫颈癌与高危型人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)的持续感染密切相关,并对女性健康构成重大威胁。邱华石汤剂(QHD)在宫颈癌 治疗中展现出潜在的治疗作用,但其作用机制尚不明确。方法:通过网络药理学筛选QHD针对HPV相关宫颈癌的核心靶点。通过整合体内和体外实验评估槲皮素的抗肿瘤效果。采用免疫荧光染色观察HPV16感染状态。同时,利用qRT-PCR和Western blot检测HPV16致癌基因E6和E7的mRNA和蛋白表达水平。免疫组织化学(IHC)用于动物组织中蛋白表达的原位验证。此外,通过Western blot定量分析PRKACA/PKA/CREB轴和核心糖酵解调节因子的关键分子蛋白水平。进一步,使用商业试剂盒评估cAMP含量、细胞葡萄糖摄取、乳酸产生以及细胞外酸化率(ECAR)和耗氧率(OCR)。此外,进行了PRKACA过表达实验以解析其在槲皮素介导效应中的调控作用。结果:网络药理学分析确定槲皮素和PRKACA为QHD对抗HPV相关宫颈癌的核心靶点。槲皮素抑制了早期HPV16感染,下调了HPV16 E6/E7的表达,并抑制了细胞增殖。机制上,槲皮素降低了细胞内cAMP水平,使cAMP/PKA/CREB信号轴失活,并抑制了关键糖酵解蛋白的表达。一致地,槲皮素抑制了糖酵解表型,包括葡萄糖摄取减少、乳酸分泌减少和ATP生成减少,同时伴随ECAR降低和OCR恢复。这些表型效应可通过PRKACA过表达逆转。结论:槲皮素通过抑制PRKACA表达来破坏cAMP/PKA/CREB/糖酵解信号轴,从而发挥其针对HPV相关宫颈癌的抗肿瘤作用,为QHD的临床应用提供了分子基础。

papers.title: A study to assess the knowledge, perceived roles and training needs of school teachers regarding human papillomavirus vaccination programs in selected schools of Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India
papers.abstract: Background: Cervical cancer is a critical global health challenge, with India bearing over 22% of worldwide mortality. School teachers are vital, trusted stakeholders who can mitigate vaccine hesitancy and champion adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) immunization. However, institutional frameworks rarely address teachers' internal educational deficits. This study evaluated the baseline health literacy, perceived roles, and training needs of school teachers in Dehradun, India. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 110 school teachers across selected government and private schools named shri guru ram rai (SGRR) public school, Government Primary School, Charan Haly Child School, Floridale School, Government Girls Inter College (GGIC), Prabhanand Children Academy, Government Inter College, and Shivalik Hills Academy in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India from Jan to June 2026 using convenience sampling. Data were gathered via self-structured, validated instruments capturing socio-demographics, knowledge, perceived roles, and training needs. An evidence-based HPV awareness pamphlet was distributed immediately following baseline assessments. Results: The cohort was predominantly female (90.9%) and lacked prior exposure to school health programs (96.4%) or HPV training (100.0%). Severe health literacy deficits were observed, with 77.3% of teachers demonstrating poor baseline knowledge. Institutional disconnect was high; 63.6% exhibited poor commitment regarding active responsibilities in vaccine promotion. Conversely, 81.8% indicated high training demands, with an exceptional overall scale mean of 4.68 out of 5.0. Notably, the highest demand (μ=4.80) was for structured educational materials (like pamphlets) to distribute during parent-teacher meetings. Conclusions: While educators possess critically low baseline clinical awareness and professional involvement regarding HPV, they demonstrate immense, proactive motivation for capacity building. Distributing targeted, evidence-based awareness pamphlets represents an affordable, highly scalable intervention to bridge institutional gaps, empower educators, and foster supportive school environments for adolescent immunization.
papers.journal: International Journal of Reproduction, Contraception, Obstetrics and Gynecology

papers.title_zh: 一项评估德里达尔恩市乌塔拉甘特邦印度选定学校中学校教师对人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种项目的知识、感知角色和培训需求的研究
papers.source_body_en: Background: Cervical cancer is a critical global health challenge, with India bearing over 22% of worldwide mortality. School teachers are vital, trusted stakeholders who can mitigate vaccine hesitancy and champion adolescent human papillomavirus (HPV) immunization. However, institutional frameworks rarely address teachers' internal educational deficits. This study evaluated the baseline health literacy, perceived roles, and training needs of school teachers in Dehradun, India. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 110 school teachers across selected government and private schools named shri guru ram rai (SGRR) public school, Government Primary School, Charan Haly Child School, Floridale School, Government Girls Inter College (GGIC), Prabhanand Children Academy, Government Inter College, and Shivalik Hills Academy in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India from Jan to June 2026 using convenience sampling. Data were gathered via self-structured, validated instruments capturing socio-demographics, knowledge, perceived roles, and training needs. An evidence-based HPV awareness pamphlet was distributed immediately following baseline assessments. Results: The cohort was predominantly female (90.9%) and lacked prior exposure to school health programs (96.4%) or HPV training (100.0%). Severe health literacy deficits were observed, with 77.3% of teachers demonstrating poor baseline knowledge. Institutional disconnect was high; 63.6% exhibited poor commitment regarding active responsibilities in vaccine promotion. Conversely, 81.8% indicated high training demands, with an exceptional overall scale mean of 4.68 out of 5.0. Notably, the highest demand (μ=4.80) was for structured educational materials (like pamphlets) to distribute during parent-teacher meetings. Conclusions: While educators possess critically low baseline clinical awareness and professional involvement regarding HPV, they demonstrate immense, proactive motivation for capacity building. Distributing targeted, evidence-based awareness pamphlets represents an affordable, highly scalable intervention to bridge institutional gaps, empower educators, and foster supportive school environments for adolescent immunization.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:宫颈癌是全球性的健康挑战,印度承担了全球死亡率的22%以上。学校教师是关键且值得信赖的利益相关者,能够缓解疫苗的犹豫态度并推动青少年人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)疫苗接种。然而,机构框架很少涉及教师内部的教育缺陷。本研究评估了印度德里达尔恩市选定学校中学校教师的基线健康素养、感知角色和培训需求。方法:采用描述性横断面研究设计,于2026年1月至6月期间,通过便利抽样方式在德里达尔恩市乌塔拉甘特邦选定的政府和私立学校(包括 shri guru ram rai(SGRR)公立学校、政府小学、Charan Haly儿童学校、Floridale学校、政府女子综合学院(GGIC)、Prabhanand儿童学院、政府综合学院和Shivalik Hills学院)中对110名学校教师进行调查。数据通过自设结构化、经过验证的工具收集,涵盖社会人口学、知识、感知角色和培训需求。在基线评估后立即分发基于证据的HPV意识传单。结果:队列研究中女性占主导地位(90.9%),且缺乏对学校健康项目(96.4%)或HPV培训(100.0%)的先前接触。观察到严重的健康素养缺陷,77.3%的教师表现出较差的基线知识水平。机构脱节现象严重,63.6%的教师在推动疫苗方面表现出较差的承诺。相反,81.8%的教师表示有较高的培训需求,整体量表均值达到4.68(满分5.0)。值得注意的是,最高需求(μ=4.80)是希望在家长教师会议上分发结构化的教育材料(如传单)。结论:尽管教育工作者在HPV方面的基线临床意识和专业参与度极低,但他们表现出巨大的、主动的能力建设意愿。分发有针对性的、基于证据的意识传单是一种经济实惠且高度可扩展的干预措施,有助于弥合机构间的差距,增强教育工作者的能力,并营造支持青少年疫苗接种的学校环境。

papers.title: Human Papillomavirus-Associated Vulvar Intraepithelial Neoplasia in an Immunocompromised Patient—When Excisional Treatment Is Not Possible
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus-associated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (HPVa VIN) is a premalignant condition. Its main risk factors include human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, smoking, and immunodeficiency. Excisional treatment is preferred, but if contraindicated, topical imiquimod may be considered. The prognosis appears to be similar after these two treatments. Still, there are few studies in women living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) to draw a conclusion in this group. We present the case of a woman living with HIV and meeting diagnostic criteria for acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), with extensive, multifocal, and recurrent HPVa VIN. Due to anesthetic contraindications, we opted for topical imiquimod treatment, with good results, achieving a complete clinical response after 18 weeks of treatment. Two months later, a clinically suspected recurrence was detected, and imiquimod was reinitiated. Complete clinical resolution was again achieved after 20 weeks of treatment, and the patient started clinical surveillance every 3 months.

papers.title: Digital Health Literacy and Parental Willingness for School-Based Human Papillomavirus Vaccination: The Importance of Online Information Searching Skill
papers.abstract: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a highly effective primary prevention measure, with over 90% efficacy in preventing cervical cancer. This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between parental health literacy and willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination in Depok City, Indonesia. Data were collected via an online self-administered questionnaire completed by 208 parents. Despite a high overall willingness rate (88.9%), significant gaps remain between general vaccine awareness and detailed operational knowledge regarding dosage and timing. Using a cross-sectional design and multivariable logistic regression, the research identifies that insufficient information exposure is the primary barrier to vaccine acceptance (AOR: 0.06; 95%CI: 0.02 – 0.22). Notably, digital health literacy, specifically proficient online information-searching skills, emerged as a critical enabler of vaccination intent. Conversely, lower skills in self-generated digital content were associated with higher willingness, suggesting a correlation between passive digital engagement and program acceptance. These findings indicate that the success of the School Children’s Immunization Month (BIAS) depends on transitioning from one-way administrative announcements to interactive, literacy-based communication strategies. Strengthening parental digital competencies and fostering structured school-based dialogues are essential to bridging the knowledge-action gap. Future research should employ longitudinal designs to evaluate the long-term impact of digital literacy interventions on actual vaccine uptake across diverse Indonesian contexts.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the relationship between parental health literacy and willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination in Depok City, Indonesia, addressing the knowledge gap in vaccine awareness and operational details.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Depok City, Indonesia, involving 208 parents, to examine the relationship between parental health literacy and willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination.
analysis.methods: Data were collected via an online self-administered questionnaire, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify barriers to vaccine acceptance.
analysis.main_results: Despite a high overall willingness rate (88.9%), significant gaps exist between general vaccine awareness and detailed operational knowledge regarding dosage and timing. Insufficient information exposure was identified as the primary barrier to vaccine acceptance (AOR: 0.06; 95%CI: 0.02 – 0.22).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that digital health literacy, specifically proficient online information-searching skills, emerged as a critical enabler of vaccination intent, while lower skills in self-generated digital content were associated with higher willingness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening parental digital competencies and fostering structured school-based dialogues are essential to bridge the knowledge-action gap and improve vaccine uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data limit the generalizability of the findings. Future research should employ longitudinal designs to evaluate the long-term impact of digital literacy interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This study in Depok City, Indonesia, found that digital health literacy, particularly online information-searching skills, is crucial for parental willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination. Despite high overall willingness, gaps in vaccine awareness and operational knowledge were identified, with insufficient information exposure being the primary barrier.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在印度尼西亚德波克市进行,涉及208名家长,以探讨家长健康素养与接受学校接种HPV 疫苗接种意愿之间的关系。

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Depok City, Indonesia, involving 208 parents, to examine the relationship between parental health literacy and willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination.
analysis_en.methods: Data were collected via an online self-administered questionnaire, and multivariable logistic regression was used to identify barriers to vaccine acceptance.
analysis_en.main_results: Despite a high overall willingness rate (88.9%), significant gaps exist between general vaccine awareness and detailed operational knowledge regarding dosage and timing. analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that digital health literacy, specifically proficient online information-searching skills, emerged as a critical enabler of vaccination intent, while lower skills in self-generated digital content were associated with higher willingness.

papers.title_zh: 数字健康素养与家长对学校接种人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种的意愿:在线信息检索技能的重要性
papers.source_body_en: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a highly effective primary prevention measure, with over 90% efficacy in preventing cervical cancer. This cross-sectional study examines the relationship between parental health literacy and willingness to accept school-based HPV vaccination in Depok City, Indonesia. Data were collected via an online self-administered questionnaire completed by 208 parents. Despite a high overall willingness rate (88.9%), significant gaps remain between general vaccine awareness and detailed operational knowledge regarding dosage and timing. Using a cross-sectional design and multivariable logistic regression, the research identifies that insufficient information exposure is the primary barrier to vaccine acceptance (AOR: 0.06; 95%CI: 0.02 – 0.22). Notably, digital health literacy, specifically proficient online information-searching skills, emerged as a critical enabler of vaccination intent. Conversely, lower skills in self-generated digital content were associated with higher willingness, suggesting a correlation between passive digital engagement and program acceptance. These findings indicate that the success of the School Children’s Immunization Month (BIAS) depends on transitioning from one-way administrative announcements to interactive, literacy-based communication strategies. Strengthening parental digital competencies and fostering structured school-based dialogues are essential to bridging the knowledge-action gap. Future research should employ longitudinal designs to evaluate the long-term impact of digital literacy interventions on actual vaccine uptake across diverse Indonesian contexts.
papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒)疫苗接种是一种高度有效的初级预防措施,可预防宫颈癌,其有效性超过90%。本横断面研究探讨了家长健康素养与接受学校接种HPV 疫苗接种意愿之间的关系,研究地点为印度尼西亚德波克市。数据通过在线自填式问卷收集,共有208名家长参与。尽管总体意愿率较高(88.9%),但家长对疫苗的一般认知与具体操作知识(如剂量和时间)之间仍存在显著差距。采用横断面设计和多变量逻辑回归分析,研究发现信息暴露不足是疫苗接受的主要障碍(AOR: 0.06;95%CI: 0.02 – 0.22)。值得注意的是,数字健康素养,特别是熟练的在线信息检索技能,被发现是疫苗接种意愿的关键促进因素。相反,较低的自生成数字内容技能则与较高的意愿相关,表明被动的数字参与与项目接受之间存在相关性。这些发现表明,学校儿童免疫月(BIAS)的成功取决于从单向行政公告向互动、基于素养的沟通策略转变。加强家长的数字能力并促进结构化的学校对话对于弥合知识与行动之间的差距至关重要。未来的研究应采用纵向设计,以评估数字素养干预措施在不同印尼背景下的长期影响对实际疫苗接种率的影响。

papers.title: Knowledge and Attitudes towards Human Papillomavirus and HPV vaccination among girls aged 9-14 years in Lira City West, Northern Uganda: A cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the necessary cause of nearly all cervical cancers and remains an important public-health problem, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Vaccination before exposure to HPV is an effective primary prevention strategy. This study assessed knowledge of HPV and HPV vaccination and attitudes towards HPV vaccination among girls aged 9–14 years attending selected primary schools in Lira City West Division, Northern Uganda. Methods: A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted among 398 girls aged 9–14 years from three high-enrolment primary schools. Participants were stratified by school and class and selected systematically within strata. Data were collected using an interviewer-administered structured questionnaire in English or Leb Lango. Sociodemographic characteristics, individual knowledge items and five-point Likert attitude items were analysed descriptively using frequencies and percentages in IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Results: Only 26.4% of participants had heard of HPV and 15.6% identified HPV as a virus associated with cervical cancer. When asked about transmission, 65.8% selected sexual contact and 14.6% selected skin-to-skin contact. Awareness of the HPV vaccine was higher, with 76.9% having heard of it and 86.7% indicating that it can prevent cervical cancer. Favourable attitudes were common: 77.9% intended to receive the vaccine, 79.4% perceived it as safe, 78.6% considered vaccination important and 77.9% would recommend it to friends. Parents or guardians influenced vaccination views among 75.1% of participants. However, 95.0% disagreed or strongly disagreed that sufficient HPV-vaccine information was available to them. Conclusion: Girls in the selected schools were generally receptive to HPV vaccination but had limited understanding of HPV infection and its relationship with cervical cancer. The findings show a mismatch between relatively high vaccine awareness and favourable attitudes, and limited HPV knowledge alongside perceived insufficiency of information. School-based vaccination should be accompanied by repeated, age-appropriate education involving girls, parents and health workers.

The findings show a mismatch between relatively high vaccine awareness and favourable attitudes, and limited HPV knowledge alongside perceived insufficiency of information. School-based vaccination should be accompanied by repeated, age-appropriate education involving girls, parents and health workers.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是几乎所有宫颈癌的必要病因,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家,仍然是重要的公共卫生问题。在接触HPV之前接种疫苗接种是一种有效的初级预防策略。本研究评估了9–14岁女孩对HPV及其疫苗接种的知识和态度,这些女孩来自乌干达北部Lira市西区的三所高入学率的初级学校。方法:在三所高入学率初级学校中,对398名9–14岁女孩进行了定量横断面研究。参与者按学校和班级进行分层,并在分层内系统抽样。数据通过英语或Leb Lango的访谈式结构化问卷收集,并使用IBM SPSS Statistics版本27进行描述性分析,包括社会人口学特征、知识项目和五点李克特量表态度项目。结果:只有26.4%的参与者听说过HPV,其中15.6%将HPV识别为与宫颈癌相关的病毒。当被问及传播的传播途径时,65.8%的参与者选择了性接触,14.6%选择了皮肤接触。对于HPV 疫苗的知晓率更高,76.9%的参与者听说过它,86.7%的参与者认为它可以预防宫颈癌。积极的态度较为普遍:77.9%的参与者表示有意接种疫苗,79.4%的参与者认为其安全,78.6%的参与者认为疫苗接种重要,77.9%的参与者会向朋友推荐它。75.1%的参与者表示父母或监护人影响了他们对疫苗接种的看法。然而,95.0%的参与者不同意或强烈不同意他们获得了足够的HPV-疫苗信息。结论:所选学校中的女孩总体上对HPV 疫苗接种持开放态度,但对HPV感染及其与宫颈癌的关系了解有限。研究结果表明,HPV 疫苗的知晓率较高与积极态度之间存在不匹配,同时HPV知识有限与信息不足的感知并存。基于学校的疫苗接种应与重复的、适合年龄的教育相结合,包括女孩、家长和卫生工作者。

papers.title: Heterologous Antigen Regimen and Bicistronic DNA Vaccination Targeting HPV16 E5 and E7 Oncoproteins: Immunoinformatics and Preclinical Antitumor Efficacy
papers.abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus, particularly HPV16, is a major cause of cervical cancer and orogenital malignancies. Therapeutic DNA vaccines targeting viral oncoproteins represent a promising strategy to induce antitumor immune responses. However, the impact of antigen combinations in bicistronic vectors and the immunization sequence on therapeutic efficacy remains poorly understood. Thus, this study aimed to characterize in silico previously described E5CP and E7CP vaccines, develop a new bicistronic construct, and evaluate its antitumor efficacy under different immunization regimens in vivo. The constructs were initially characterized regarding predicted physicochemical, immunological, and structural properties, followed by molecular confirmation of plasmid construction and qualitative assessment of transcript detection after transient transfection. In vivo, C57BL/6 mice bearing C3 tumors were immunized with five different regimens combining the monocistronic or bicistronic constructs. At the endpoint, tumors and spleens were collected for histopathological and immunological analyses. The results showed that regimens using the bicistronic construct or including E5 in the first dose were associated with lower mean tumor volumes or delayed tumor growth compared to the control groups. Histopathological and immunophenotypic changes were variable among regimens, and an exploratory analysis suggested an association between lower nitric oxide levels and smaller tumor volumes. Therefore, the order of antigen administration and the use of bicistronic constructs warrant further investigation as strategies that could be optimized to improve the therapeutic efficacy of HPV DNA vaccines.
authors: Keyla Aparecida Alves de Sá Carneiro Melo

papers.title: NavDx (ctHPVDNA) recurrence detection in surgically treated human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV+)-positivity in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is a favorable prognostic indicator though 10–25% of patients will experience progressive disease within 3 years of treatment. This project assesses the validity of circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance in patients following definitive surgical treatment. A retrospective review of patients with HPV+ OPSCC treated with definitive resection at a single institution between 2020 and 2023 was performed. Patients underwent standard post treatment imaging (CT neck and chest and/or PET/CT). ctHPVDNA samples were also collected. Imaging response was assessed via NI-RADS (Neck Imaging Reporting and Data System) risk classification and independently reviewed. The cohort included 16 patients (15 primary, 1 recurrent): 81% males; median age 58; 56% never smokers, 38% former smokers, 6% current smokers; 63% tonsil primary, 31% BOT; 38% T1, 19% T2, 44% Tx; 0% N0, 25% N1, 38% N2a, 31% N2b, 0% N2c, 6% N3 (AJCC 7th edition). Four patients (25%) experienced biopsy-proven recurrence (13% locoregional, 13% distant) with a median time to recurrence of 14 months (range 3–42). NI-RADS suggested 4 locoregional recurrences (1 true positive, 3 false positive) yielding 50% sensitivity, 75% specificity, 25% PPV, 90% NPV. ctHPVDNA identified 2 locoregional events, and 2 distant events (4 true positive, 0 false positive) yielding 100% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, 100%. Surveillance ctHPVDNA more accurately identified recurrences with minimal false positives compared to post-treatment imaging, which may limit the need for repeat imaging and unwarranted salvage operations which increase patient worry, morbidity, and financial toxicity.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the recurrence detection in surgically treated human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) using circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance. The central question is whether ctHPVDNA is a more accurate method for identifying recurrences compared to standard post-treatment imaging.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes a retrospective review of patients with HPV+ OPSCC who underwent definitive resection at a single institution between 2020 and 2023. ctHPVDNA samples were collected alongside standard post-treatment imaging (CT neck and chest and/or PET/CT). Imaging response was assessed via NI-RADS risk classification and independently reviewed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ctHPVDNA surveillance more accurately identified recurrences with minimal false positives compared to post-treatment imaging. This suggests that ctHPVDNA could potentially reduce the need for repeat imaging and unnecessary salvage operations, thereby decreasing patient worry, morbidity, and financial toxicity.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Post-treatment imaging via NI-RADS had 50% sensitivity and 75% specificity, with 25% false positives. ctHPVDNA showed 100% sensitivity and specificity, but the evidence is limited to a single institution and a small cohort of 16 patients. There is no mention of long-term outcomes or broader applicability.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to validate the utility of ctHPVDNA surveillance in larger, multi-institutional cohorts and to assess its long-term effectiveness. Additionally, studies should explore the integration of ctHPVDNA into routine clinical practice for recurrence monitoring in HPV-associated OPSCC.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the use of circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance for detecting recurrence in surgically treated human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). A retrospective study of 16 patients (2020–2023) found that ctHPVDNA identified all recurrences with 100% sensitivity and specificity, whereas post-treatment imaging via NI-RADS had 50% sensitivity and 75% specificity. The findings suggest that ctHPVDNA may offer more accurate recurrence detection with fewer false positives, potentially reducing the need for repeat imaging and unnecessary salvage procedures. However, the evidence is limited to a single institution and small cohort, highlighting the need for larger, multi-center studies to confirm these results and assess long-term clinical utility.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于使用循环肿瘤HPV DNA(ctHPVDNA) 监测检测手术治疗后与人乳头瘤病毒相关的口咽部鳞状细胞癌(OPSCC)的复发情况。核心问题是ctHPVDNA是否比标准的术后治疗影像学检查更准确地识别复发。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 证据基础包括对2020年至2023年间某单一机构接受根治性切除术治疗的HPV+ OPSCC患者的回顾性分析。同时收集了ctHPVDNA样本和标准的术后治疗影像学检查(颈部和胸部CT以及/或PET/CT)。影像学反应通过NI-RADS风险分类进行评估,并由独立评审进行确认。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ctHPVDNA 监测在检测复发方面比术后治疗影像学更为准确,且假阳性较少。这表明ctHPVDNA可能减少重复影像学检查和不必要的挽救性手术,从而降低患者的焦虑、发病率和经济负担。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 术后治疗影像学通过NI-RADS评估具有50%的灵敏度和75%的特异性,假阳性率为25%。ctHPVDNA表现出100%的灵敏度和特异性,但证据仅限于单一机构和16例患者的队列研究。未提及长期结果或更广泛的应用性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步研究以验证ctHPVDNA 监测在更大规模、多机构的队列研究中的实用性,并评估其长期效果。此外,应研究ctHPVDNA在HPV相关OPSCC复发监测中的临床整合应用。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the recurrence detection in surgically treated human papillomavirus-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) using circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance. The central question is whether ctHPVDNA is a more accurate method for identifying recurrences compared to standard post-treatment imaging.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes a retrospective review of patients with HPV+ OPSCC who underwent definitive resection at a single institution between 2020 and 2023. ctHPVDNA samples were collected alongside standard post-treatment imaging (CT neck and chest and/or PET/CT). Imaging response was assessed via NI-RADS risk classification and independently reviewed.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ctHPVDNA surveillance more accurately identified recurrences with minimal false positives compared to post-treatment imaging. This suggests that ctHPVDNA could potentially reduce the need for repeat imaging and unnecessary salvage operations, thereby decreasing patient worry, morbidity, and financial toxicity.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Post-treatment imaging via NI-RADS had 50% sensitivity and 75% specificity, with 25% false positives. ctHPVDNA showed 100% sensitivity and specificity, but the evidence is limited to a single institution and a small cohort of 16 patients. There is no mention of long-term outcomes or broader applicability.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to validate the utility of ctHPVDNA surveillance in larger, multi-institutional cohorts and to assess its long-term effectiveness. Additionally, studies should explore the integration of ctHPVDNA into routine clinical practice for recurrence monitoring in HPV-associated OPSCC.

papers.title_zh: NavDx (ctHPVDNA)在手术治疗的与人乳头瘤病毒相关的口咽部鳞状细胞癌中复发检测
papers.source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV+)-positivity in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is a favorable prognostic indicator though 10–25% of patients will experience progressive disease within 3 years of treatment. This project assesses the validity of circulating tumor HPV DNA (ctHPVDNA) surveillance in patients following definitive surgical treatment. A retrospective review of patients with HPV+ OPSCC treated with definitive resection at a single institution between 2020 and 2023 was performed. Patients underwent standard post treatment imaging (CT neck and chest and/or PET/CT). ctHPVDNA samples were also collected. Imaging response was assessed via NI-RADS (Neck Imaging Reporting and Data System) risk classification and independently reviewed. The cohort included 16 patients (15 primary, 1 recurrent): 81% males; median age 58; 56% never smokers, 38% former smokers, 6% current smokers; 63% tonsil primary, 31% BOT; 38% T1, 19% T2, 44% Tx; 0% N0, 25% N1, 38% N2a, 31% N2b, 0% N2c, 6% N3 (AJCC 7th edition). Four patients (25%) experienced biopsy-proven recurrence (13% locoregional, 13% distant) with a median time to recurrence of 14 months (range 3–42). NI-RADS suggested 4 locoregional recurrences (1 true positive, 3 false positive) yielding 50% sensitivity, 75% specificity, 25% PPV, 90% NPV. ctHPVDNA identified 2 locoregional events, and 2 distant events (4 true positive, 0 false positive) yielding 100% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% PPV, 100%. Surveillance ctHPVDNA more accurately identified recurrences with minimal false positives compared to post-treatment imaging, which may limit the need for repeat imaging and unwarranted salvage operations which increase patient worry, morbidity, and financial toxicity.

Adds StockTitan as a preferred source · opens Google Add on Google Not now 09/28/2026 - 12:20 PM New U.S. patent expands intellectual property foundation for DARE-HPV, a potential first-in-category treatment targeting persistent high-risk HPV infection DARE-HPV Phase 2 study underway with topline results expected in 2027; program supported by approximately $10 million in non-dilutive ARPA-H funding and a $2.0 million NIAID award DARE-HPV is designed to address a major treatment gap for the millions of U.S. women who experience high-risk HPV infection each year, for which there is currently no FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment SAN DIEGO, Sept. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Daré Bioscience, Inc. (NASDAQ: DARE), a purpose-driven health biotech company solely focused on closing the gap in women's health between promising science and real-world solutions, today announced the issuance of U.S. Patent No. 12,678,439, titled “Lopinavir and Ritonavir for the Treatment of Cervix Disorders,” which covers pharmaceutical compositions formulated for topical application comprising lopinavir and ritonavir for the treatment of HPV-related cervical pathologies. The patent, issued by the United States Patent and Trademark Office on July 14, 2026, to Douglas Pharmaceuticals Limited, a licensor to Daré Bioscience, describes pharmaceutical compositions containing therapeutically effective amounts of lopinavir and ritonavir, including specific lopinavir-to-ritonavir weight ratios and formulations designed for topical administration. The patent includes claims directed to compositions for treating or inhibiting the development of early-stage neoplasias and for treating or preventing HPV-related cervical neoplasias. The patent is expected to provide protection into at least 2039. “This patent adds another important layer to the foundation we are building around DARE-HPV at a particularly exciting point in the program’s development,” said Sabrina Martucci Johnson, President and CEO of Daré Bioscience. “Millions of women experience high-risk HPV infection each year in the United States, yet there is still no FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment to clear the infection. DARE-HPV is designed to change that paradigm with a localized, self-administered, non-surgical approach, and our Phase 2 study is now evaluating its potential to do exactly that. With clinical development underway, significant non-dilutive funding supporting the program, and an expanded intellectual property position, we believe DARE-HPV represents a compelling opportunity to address a significant unmet need in women’s health and, if successful and approved, potentially establishing the first FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment for HPV infection.” The patent adds to the intellectual property landscape supporting the development of DARE-HPV, Daré Bioscience’s investigational proprietary fixed-dose formulation of lopinavir and ritonavir in a soft gel vaginal insert being developed as a potential treatment for persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Daré holds an exclusive U.S. license to the patent described above and the broader patent family related to DARE-HPV under its 2023 license agreement with Douglas Pharmaceuticals Limited. DARE-HPV is currently being evaluated in a Phase 2 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical study in approximately 100 women with confirmed persistent high-risk HPV infection (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07601074). The study is designed to evaluate the safety and antiviral activity of lower and higher doses of DARE-HPV compared with placebo over an up to 21-day course of daily treatment, with HPV clearance at three months post-treatment as the primary endpoint. Topline results are expected in 2027. DARE-HPV is being developed as a non-surgical, localized, self-administered therapy designed to clear persistent high-risk HPV infection. There are currently no FDA-approved pharmacologic treatments for HPV infection. Daré Bioscience’s development of DARE-HPV is supported by approximately $10 million in non-dilutive funding from the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) as Sprint for Women’s Health awardee, and a $2.0 million award granted by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) of the National Institutes of Health (Award Number R44AI188623). ABOUT DARE-HPV DARE-HPV is an investigational, proprietary fixed-dose formulation of lopinavir and ritonavir in a soft gel vaginal insert being developed as a potential non-surgical, localized, self-administered treatment for persistent high-risk HPV infection. Lopinavir and ritonavir are protease inhibitors with established antiviral activity. HPV infection is the underlying cause of virtually all cervical cancer cases in the United States. An estimated six million women per year in the United States experience high-risk HPV infection, for which there are currently no FDA-approved pharmacologic treatments. If clinically successful and approved, DARE-HPV could be the first FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment for HPV infection. ABOUT DARÉ BIOSCIENCE, INC. Daré Bioscience (NASDAQ: DARE) is a purpose-driven health biotech company solely focused on closing the gap in women’s health between promising science and real-world solutions. Every innovation Daré Bioscience advances is based in advanced science and backed by rigorous, peer-reviewed research. From contraception to menopause, sexual health to fertility, vaginal health to infectious disease, Daré Bioscience is working to close critical gaps in care using science that serves her needs. For decades, women have been told to “wait it out” or “live with it,” while innovations that could improve their quality of life languish in the regulatory or funding pipeline. With growing awareness around menopause, sexual health, and vaginal health, the conversation is shifting. However, access to proven solutions is lagging. Daré Bioscience is working to change that. Learn more at darebioscience.com. analysis.brief_en: Dare Bioscience has announced a newly issued U.S. patent for topical lopinavir and ritonavir formulations targeting HPV-related cervical conditions. The patent, number 12,678,439, was granted to Douglas Pharmaceuticals on July 14, 2026, and is expected to provide patent protection until at least 2039. The company is developing DARE-HPV, a soft gel vaginal insert, as a potential first FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment for high-risk HPV infection. A Phase 2 study is currently testing lower and higher doses of DARE-HPV in approximately 100 women with persistent high-risk HPV infection. The study is randomized, placebo-controlled, and double-blind, with the primary endpoint being HPV clearance three months after treatment. Topline results are anticipated in 2027. Currently, no pharmacologic treatment for HPV infection is FDA-approved, and the success of DARE-HPV depends on clinical outcomes and regulatory approval. The development is supported by $10 million in non-dilutive ARPA-H funding and a $2.0 million NIAID award. The report highlights the significance of the patent and the ongoing clinical trial for potential future treatment options.

Ask questions, get summaries, explore topics.Instantly. In 62 patients with ICI-naive HPV16-Positive HNSCC, 17.7% experienced grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events. Advertisement Among 53 ICI-naive patients in the modified intent-to-treat (ITT) population, central review identified 6 complete responses and 12 partial responses. The HPV16-targeted immunotherapy PDS0101 combined with pembrolizumab (Keytruda) produced a central review-assessed objective response rate (ORR) of 33.96% (95% CI, 21.52%-48.27%) and a median overall survival (OS) of 39.3 months (95% CI, 23.90-not evaluable [NE]) among patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)–naive, HPV16-positive recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), according to results from the phase 2 VERSATILE-002 trial (NCT04260126) published in JAMA Oncology.1 A separate ICI-resistant cohort had no objective responses and did not meet its primary end point. What were the results in the ICI-naive cohort? Among 53 ICI-naive patients in the modified intent-to-treat (ITT) population, central review identified 6 complete responses and 12 partial responses. The investigator-assessed ORR was 35.85% (95% CI, 23.14%-50.20%). The disease control rate was 60.4%, and the median duration of response was not evaluable (NE; 95% CI, 6.9 months-NE). Tumor reductions of more than 90% occurred in 22.6% of patients. The median progression-free survival (PFS) was 5.3 months (95% CI, 2.10-9.00) by central review. At a median follow-up of 24.4 months (IQR, 9.7-29.5), the 12- and 24-month OS rates were 78.5% (95% CI, 64.5%-87.5%) and 67.6% (95% CI, 52.5%-78.8%), respectively. In an exploratory analysis, patients with a PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) of 1 to 19 had a median OS of 29.5 months. How effective was the regimen in the ICI-resistant cohort? Among 22 patients in the ICI-resistant cohort, no objective responses were observed. The median PFS was 2.0 months (95% CI, 1.4-2.1), and the median OS was 14.8 months (95% CI, 8.5-26.0). The investigators wrote that this finding is consistent with evidence that ICIs are most effective when given early. Later on, tumors may lose the antigen presentation machinery that both pembrolizumab and PDS0101 depend on. What was the safety profile of PDS0101 plus pembrolizumab? In the ICI-naive safety population of 62 patients, 17.7% experienced grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). One grade 4 event, encephalitis, occurred approximately 1 year after the last PDS0101 dose and was deemed related to pembrolizumab but unrelated to PDS0101. No grade 5 TRAEs occurred. Across all 87 treated patients, the rate of grade 3 or higher TRAEs was 13.8%. The most common TRAEs in the ICI-naive cohort were injection site pain (59.7%), fatigue (40.3%), and injection site swelling (30.6%). All injection site reactions were grade 1 or 2. AEs led to discontinuation of PDS0101 in 6.5% of patients and of pembrolizumab in 11.3%. What is the VERSATILE-002 trial design? The open-label, multicenter trial used a Simon 2-stage design and enrolled 88 patients across 26 centers in the US, UK, and Ireland between March 2021 and May 2025. ICI-naive patients were required to have a PD-L1 CPS of 1 or greater. ICI-resistant patients had disease progression after at least 8 weeks of prior ICI therapy. Patients received pembrolizumab at 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles, plus subcutaneous PDS0101 at 1 mL on cycles 1, 2, 3, 4, and 12. The primary end point was ORR per RECIST v1.1 by masked independent central review. Secondary end points included PFS, OS, and safety. PDS0101 combines a T cell–activating lipid platform with HPV16 E6 and E7 multiepitope peptides. It is designed to induce HPV16-specific CD4 and CD8 T-cell responses. What are the next steps for PDS0101 in head and neck cancer? The investigators concluded that the findings support further evaluation of the combination in the first-line setting. “These results support the durable clinical effect of PDS0101, consistent with promising survival outcomes reported in 2 other recently published studies, the IMMUNOCERV study [NCT04580771], and the NCI-led study in HPV16-positive recurrent and/or metastatic cancers,” said Kirk Shepard, MD, chief medical officer of PDS Biotech, in a press release on the VERSATILE-002 findings.2 References Weiss J, Kaczmar J, Chintakuntlawar A, et al. GOOD LIFE OHAYO PINAS News Last updated October 1, 2026, 11:39 AM Lawmakers push expanded HPV vaccination for boys By Jimbo Gulle October 1, 2026, 11:39 AM Share Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Female lawmakers, health advocates and partners attend the launch of the HPV Prevention Policy Atlas Asia-Pacific 2026 at the House of Representatives. Discussions focused on strengthening HPV prevention in the Philippines, including expanding vaccination to boys and making greater use of Gender and Development funds. (Courtesy James Daniel Danio) Resize Text:16px Estimated reading time: 2 minutes and 18 seconds Lawmakers and health advocates are urging the Philippines to expand its human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination program to include boys and make greater use of Gender and Development (GAD) funds for cervical cancer prevention and early detection. LegislativeBranch The recommendations emerged during the launch of the HPV Prevention Policy Atlas Asia-Pacific 2026 at the House of Representatives, where lawmakers, health advocates, civil society groups and cervical cancer survivors discussed gaps in HPV prevention policies and implementation. - Advertisement - Discover more Legislators vaccine Vaccines & Immunizations The Philippines scored 71.6 percent, rated “Good” in the Atlas, but trailed several Southeast Asian neighbors in the assessment of national HPV prevention policies. The findings also pointed to gaps in coverage, with HPV vaccination among females remaining below 30 percent and cervical cancer screening participation below 15 percent. HPV is a common virus associated with cervical cancer and other cancers affecting both women and men. Vaccination and early detection are key measures in preventing HPV-related diseases. Push for gender-neutral HPV vaccination Under the Department of Health’s school-based immunization program, the quadrivalent HPV vaccine is provided to eligible female public school students aged 9 to 14. Health experts at the forum called for consideration of gender-neutral vaccination to extend protection to boys, noting that several countries with established HPV prevention policies vaccinate both girls and boys. European Parliamentary Forum for Sexual and Reproductive Rights Executive Director Neil Datta said boys can also contract HPV and develop related cancers. MedicalLiterature & Resources “You can only achieve the elimination of HPV if you also vaccinate boys. That’s the first thing to consider,” Datta said. Vaccinating boys would provide direct protection against HPV-related diseases and help reduce transmission of the virus, he added. Albay 1st District Rep. Cielo Krisel Lagman, chair of the Philippine Legislators’ Committee on Population and Development Foundation, said Congress has consistently supported vaccine funding but stressed that appropriations must translate into actual access. “The policy is only as good as the implementation. Even if it is good on paper, but it is not implemented, even if there is funding but it is not used in the right and appropriate way, nothing will happen,” Lagman said. GAD funds for prevention Lagman also cited the potential of GAD funds to support cervical cancer prevention and early detection, including HPV vaccination, screening and other women’s health services. She called for better use of existing government resources to address barriers to access, particularly for families in remote communities that face transportation expenses and other out-of-pocket costs. Lagman also urged wider access to vaccination, screening and treatment through existing health financing mechanisms. The Atlas assesses policies on HPV vaccination, cervical cancer screening and access to health information. Participants said closing the gap between policy and protection would require adequate funding, stronger implementation and broader access to preventive services. - Advertisement - Discover more Infectious Diseases Legislative Branch Cancer Leave a review Tags Cervical Cancer Prevention GAD Funds Gender-Neutral HPV Vaccination HPV Prevention Policy Atlas 2026 HPV Vaccination Philippines Right Banner RECENT STORIES ‘No sign of deception,’ NBI says of Gracioso lie detector test results News October 1, 2026, 5:47 PM SC junks bid challenging Senate June 3 session News October 1, 2026, 4:35 PM Palace: OSG ready to defend BSKE reset before SC News October 1, 2026, 3:59 PM Veloso urges Filipinos to follow legal recruitment processes News October 1, 2026, 3:39 PM Petitioners mull review after SC junks threshold challenge News October 1, 2026, 3:35 PM Scroll to play 🔇 Tap for Sound Popular Categories NewsBusinessSpotlightSportsWorldPhotosShowbiz - Advertisement - Previous article Bank loans, money supply posted faster growth in August 2026 Next article Luxury Bohol resort shuts down after LandBank foreclosure ✓ Thanks for sharing! supplementary_news.content: Menu SECTIONS News Features CME Clinical Tools Conferences Special Collections Multimedia Diagnosis & Disease Info Clinical Quiz Fact Sheets Topics Axial Spondyloarthritis Connective Tissue Disease Crystal Arthropathies Diseases of Bone and Cartilage General Medicine General Rheumatology Infection in Rheumatic Disease Musculoskeletal Pain Myositis Osteoarthritis Pediatric Rheumatology Practice Management Psoriatic Arthritis Rheumatoid Arthritis Sjögren Syndrome Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Vasculitis Haymarket Medical Network Cancer Therapy Advisor Clinical Advisor Clinical Pain Advisor Dermatology Advisor Endocrinology Advisor Gastroenterology Advisor Hematology Advisor Infectious Disease Advisor Medical Bag MPR Neurology Advisor Obesity Advisor Oncology Nurse Advisor Ophthalmology Advisor Optometry Advisor Psychiatry Advisor Pulmonology Advisor Rare Disease Advisor Renal and Urology News Rheumatology Advisor Sleep Wake Advisor The Cardiology Advisor Vaccine Advisor Search for: Part of the News and Features CME Conferences Clinical Tools Special Collections Multimedia Share this article Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share by Email Print General Rheumatology Cervical Cancer Screening Gaps Persist in Women With Immune-Mediated Inflammatory Disease Ryner Lai, MBBS | Publish Date September 28, 2026 Prolonged use of biologic therapy and missed cervical cancer screenings are associated with an increased prevalence of multiple high-risk human papillomavirus infections among patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) was found in approximately one-fifth of patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases who were not up to date with cervical cancer screening, according to a study published in Rheumatic & Musculoskeletal Diseases. Epidemiological studies suggest that HPV is the most common sexually transmitted infection worldwide and is responsible for virtually all cervical cancers. In particular, women with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases are at increased risk of developing cervical neoplasia, although the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. While current guidelines recommend regular cervical cancer screening, uptake among patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases is relatively low. Researchers therefore sought to better understand cervical cancer risk among this cohort. They collected relevant clinical information from women with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, including HPV vaccination status, sexual behaviors, and comorbidities. Vaginal self-sampling was used for sample collection. The primary outcome was high-risk HPV prevalence; secondary outcomes included the frequency of multiple high-risk HPV infections and infection persistence, defined as 2 consecutive positive vaginal self-sampling results obtained 1 year apart. These data underline the need for multidisciplinary preventive strategies integrating rheumatologists, gynecologists, primary care physicians and public health programs to optimize HPV vaccination coverage and cervical cancer prevention. A total of 485 patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases were eligible for cervical cancer screening. Among these patients, 296 were not up to date with their screening. Of these 296 patients, 276 (mean age, 48±10 years) consented to vaginal self-screening. Most patients (74%) had autoimmune connective tissue diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus (30%) and systemic sclerosis (22%). Among patients who performed vaginal self-screening, 20% tested positive for at least 1 high-risk HPV type. Researchers identified an inverse correlation with age: 29% of women aged 30 to 40 years tested positive, compared with 12% of women aged 51 to 60 years. Researchers also found that 35% of patients — 19 of 55 patients who tested positive for at least one high-risk HPV type — harbored more than 2 high-risk HPV infections. Results of multivariate analysis showed that both the number of lifetime sexual partners (odds ratio [OR], 1.19) and age at first sexual intercourse (OR, 0.85) were associated with high-risk HPV infection. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that duration of biologic therapy was independently associated with multiple high-risk HPV infections (OR, 1.57). “Collectively, these data underline the need for multidisciplinary preventive strategies integrating rheumatologists, gynecologists, primary care physicians and public health programmes to optimise HPV vaccination coverage and cervical cancer prevention in high-risk populations,” the researchers concluded. Some study authors may have declared affiliations with biotech, pharmaceutical, or device companies. Please see the original reference for a full list of authors’ disclosures. References: Goulenok T, Sierra C, Florence AM, et al. Prevalence and risk factors for high-risk human papillomavirus infection in patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases: a prospective study. HPV causes nearly all cases of cervical cancer and about 70% of some forms of head and neck cancers. While some regions of the United States have relatively high rates of HPV vaccination, there are major vaccine shortages in much of the world. A new Yale study, published Sept. 30 in Science Advances, introduces a genetic platform that could be used to boost future HPV vaccine development. “The current vaccine is great, there’s just not enough of it,” says Daniel DiMaio, MD PhD, Waldemar Von Zedtwitz Professor of Genetics at Yale School of Medicine (YSM). “There are persistent vaccine shortages that are anticipated to continue for the foreseeable future. Therefore, there would be a real advantage to coming up with ways to make more vaccines or make them more efficiently.” Growing HPV in bulk To create a better vaccine, DiMaio and his lab members homed in on a molecule—called the L1 protein—that's part of the virus-like particle used in the HPV vaccine. They reasoned that they could look for and isolate different versions of the L1 protein that might enable better vaccines. But there was a problem—there were no methods that allowed them to do that. So, they set about to develop a technique to isolate better versions of the L1 protein. The first step was to overcome how difficult HPV is to cultivate. “For other viruses, like influenza or SARS, we can cultivate a virus stock by letting the viruses reproduce in host cells we grow in the laboratory,” says DiMaio, a member of Yale Cancer Center. “But HPV will not reproduce in these simulated conditions. That has hindered the study of HPV, and that’s one of the barriers we had to overcome." To address these challenges, DiMaio and his lab first set out to develop a procedure to cultivate and manipulate large quantities of the HPV virus. Luckily, the researchers had two advantages, says DiMaio: a long-term grant from the National Cancer Institute, which gave them time to explore, and Yuka Takeo, PhD, a postdoctoral researcher and the paper’s first author. “When we started this project, we didn't know if it would work,” says Takeo. “As a researcher, it's risky to have a project that might not produce a result. But we cared about this.” For several years, DiMaio and Takeo looked for ways to overcome HPV’s unique biology in order to grow it in culture. HPV is composed of DNA packaged in a protein shell consisting of L1 and L2 proteins. When the researchers tried to grow the virus with L1 and L2 expressed from the same piece of DNA, called a plasmid, the plasmid was unstable and could not produce a virus. One of their breakthroughs came when they realized that if they expressed L1 and L2 from different plasmids, the plasmid stabilized and they could grow the virus. “The size of the plasmid was very important because HPV can only package small pieces of DNA,” says Takeo. “It was a breakthrough for us to have L1 and L2 on their own, small plasmids.” Developing a library of HPV mutants Being able to cultivate HPV solved one of the challenges in vaccine development. Having a version of HPV that doesn’t require refrigeration or that assembles more efficiently would solve others. But that would require different HPV variants than those currently used in the vaccine. To find a virus variant with a particular characteristic, such as being shelf-stable, researchers create thousands of random mutants and put them through a selection process. HPV mutants are made by adding mutated plasmids to cells. This introduces mutations to the virus population, but it does so randomly; most viruses will contain a mutated piece of DNA that does not match the mutant L1 protein in that same virus. DiMaio and Takeo needed a way to ensure a match between the mutation in the packaged DNA and the mutant L1 protein within the virus particle. “If the mutant protein and the mutated DNA in the virus particle do not match, you can't select for that mutant,” explains DiMaio. “We had to partition each one of these thousands or millions of mutations into the appropriate virus so that we could evaluate each mutation separately.” After close to five years of tests, the team found a way to ensure that each mutant virus contained only the matched mutant DNA. First, they exposed HPV to thousands of pieces of DNA, each with a different mutation, and the viruses took in the mutant DNA randomly. Then, they introduced the virus to cultures of human kidney cells in small enough amounts that each kidney cell could be infected by only a single virus. The virus would then undergo its natural life cycle, reproducing within the kidney cell. “We infected cells, and we recovered viruses that we hoped were enriched for particular mutants,” says DiMaio. Pulling one mutant from the library Through this work, the researchers built a library of mutants. The next step was to demonstrate that they could pull just one mutant out of their library. This test would help them determine if they could someday pull a mutant out to use in a vaccine. For the test, they aimed to show that they could select a mutant with a specific characteristic, in this case antibiotic resistance. When they modified the HPV plasmids, they attached a gene that would make the virus resistant to specific antibodies. Then they exposed the mutant library to the antibodies and infected cells. Rare mutant viruses survived, and further testing confirmed they were indeed mutants resistant to those specific antibodies. This confirmed to Takeo and DiMaio that they could select mutant with desired properties from their library. There is a long way to go before this technology can be used to develop the next HPV vaccine. But this new platform pushes the boundaries of what was previously thought possible and establishes the first system to use genetic selection for HPV. The lab is now working to select mutants that make more stable vaccines. “We began this work because we wanted to study how the virus grows,” says DiMaio. “Now that we have developed a way to select mutants, this approach could eventually lead to more or better vaccines or even antiviral agents.” Original release: https://medicine.yale.edu/news-article/cultivating-hpv-to-improve-vaccine-development/ Request an Expert MEDIA CONTACT Register for reporter access to contact details CITATIONS Science Advances TYPE OF ARTICLE Research Results SECTION MEDICINE CHANNELS All Journal News Biotech Cancer Genetics Healthcare Public Health Vaccines Women's Health Vaccines KEYWORDS HPV Vaccine Development Cervical Cancer genetic platform virus cultivation mutant variants Healthcare Access adolescent vaccination Shares COMMENTS | COMMENTING POLICY × Connecting Research and Experts with Journalists Unlock Your Access to Newswise Research News including Embargoed News and Expert Pitches 9 AM Daily Wire (click to select custom wire) 0:00 Eastern Standard Time1:00 Eastern Standard Time2:00 Eastern Standard Time3:00 Eastern Standard Time4:00 Eastern Standard Time5:00 Eastern Standard Time6:00 Eastern Standard Time7:00 Eastern Standard Time8:00 Eastern Standard Time9:00 Eastern Standard Time10:00 Eastern Standard Time11:00 Eastern Standard Time12:00 Eastern Standard Time13:00 Eastern Standard Time14:00 Eastern Standard Time15:00 Eastern Standard Time16:00 Eastern Standard Time17:00 Eastern Standard Time18:00 Eastern Standard Time19:00 Eastern Standard Time20:00 Eastern Standard Time21:00 Eastern Standard Time22:00 Eastern Standard Time23:00 Eastern Standard Time Name: Email: Media Outlet: Continue Reading Used only to deliver research news. Full Release New U.S. patent expands intellectual property foundation for DARE-HPV, a potential first-in-category treatment targeting persistent high-risk HPV infection DARE-HPV Phase 2 study underway with topline results expected in 2027; program supported by approximately $10 million in non-dilutive ARPA-H funding and a $2.0 million NIAID award DARE-HPV is designed to address a major treatment gap for the millions of U.S. women who experience high-risk HPV infection each year, for which there is currently no FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment SAN DIEGO, Sept. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Daré Bioscience, Inc. (NASDAQ: DARE), a purpose-driven health biotech company solely focused on closing the gap in women's health between promising science and real-world solutions, today announced the issuance of U.S. Patent No. 12,678,439, titled “ Lopinavir and Ritonavir for the Treatment of Cervix Disorders ,” which covers pharmaceutical compositions formulated for topical application comprising lopinavir and ritonavir for the treatment of HPV-related cervical pathologies. The patent, issued by the United States Patent and Trademark Office on July 14, 2026, to Douglas Pharmaceuticals Limited, a licensor to Daré Bioscience, describes pharmaceutical compositions containing therapeutically effective amounts of lopinavir and ritonavir, including specific lopinavir-to-ritonavir weight ratios and formulations designed for topical administration. The patent includes claims directed to compositions for treating or inhibiting the development of early-stage neoplasias and for treating or preventing HPV-related cervical neoplasias. The patent is expected to provide protection into at least 2039. “This patent adds another important layer to the foundation we are building around DARE-HPV at a particularly exciting point in the program’s development,” said Sabrina Martucci Johnson, President and CEO of Daré Bioscience. “Millions of women experience high-risk HPV infection each year in the United States, yet there is still no FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment to clear the infection. DARE-HPV is designed to change that paradigm with a localized, self-administered, non-surgical approach, and our Phase 2 study is now evaluating its potential to do exactly that. With clinical development underway, significant non-dilutive funding supporting the program, and an expanded intellectual property position, we believe DARE-HPV represents a compelling opportunity to address a significant unmet need in women’s health and, if successful and approved, potentially establishing the first FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment for HPV infection.” The patent adds to the intellectual property landscape supporting the development of DARE-HPV, Daré Bioscience’s investigational proprietary fixed-dose formulation of lopinavir and ritonavir in a soft gel vaginal insert being developed as a potential treatment for persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. Daré holds an exclusive U.S. license to the patent described above and the broader patent family related to DARE-HPV under its 2023 license agreement with Douglas Pharmaceuticals Limited. DARE-HPV is currently being evaluated in a Phase 2 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical study in approximately 100 women with confirmed persistent high-risk HPV infection (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07601074). The study is designed to evaluate the safety and antiviral activity of lower and higher doses of DARE-HPV compared with placebo over an up to 21-day course of daily treatment, with HPV clearance at three months post-treatment as the primary endpoint. Topline results are expected in 2027. DARE-HPV is being developed as a non-surgical, localized, self-administered therapy designed to clear persistent high-risk HPV infection. There are currently no FDA-approved pharmacologic treatments for HPV infection. Daré Bioscience’s development of DARE-HPV is supported by approximately $10 million in non-dilutive funding from the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) as Sprint for Women’s Health awardee, and a $2.0 million award granted by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) of the National Institutes of Health (Award Number R44AI188623). ABOUT DARE-HPV DARE-HPV is an investigational, proprietary fixed-dose formulation of lopinavir and ritonavir in a soft gel vaginal insert being developed as a potential non-surgical, localized, self-administered treatment for persistent high-risk HPV infection. Lopinavir and ritonavir are protease inhibitors with established antiviral activity. HPV infection is the underlying cause of virtually all cervical cancer cases in the United States. An estimated six million women per year in the United States experience high-risk HPV infection, for which there are currently no FDA-approved pharmacologic treatments. If clinically successful and approved, DARE-HPV could be the first FDA-approved pharmacologic treatment for HPV infection. ABOUT DARÉ BIOSCIENCE, INC. Daré Bioscience (NASDAQ: DARE) is a purpose-driven health biotech company solely focused on closing the gap in women’s health between promising science and real-world solutions. Every innovation Daré Bioscience advances is based in advanced science and backed by rigorous, peer-reviewed research. From contraception to menopause, sexual health to fertility, vaginal health to infectious disease, Daré Bioscience is working to close critical gaps in care using science that serves her needs. For decades, women have been told to “wait it out” or “live with it,” while innovations that could improve their quality of life languish in the regulatory or funding pipeline. With growing awareness around menopause, sexual health, and vaginal health, the conversation is shifting. However, access to proven solutions is lagging. Daré Bioscience is working to change that.
